newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's life insurers may sell securities - agency.
newsitem.headline: Japan's life insurers may sell securities - agency.

text.p: The chairman of the Life Insurance Association of Japan, Kenjiro Hata, said on Friday that some life insurers may sell securities, such as domestic and foreign bonds and stocks, if Tokyo stock prices do not recover, Jiji news agency reported.
Hata, also president of Meiji Life Insurance Co, was quoted as saying that possible securities sales would be aimed at realising profits before the end of the current business year on March 31.

Jiji also quoted Hata as saying that insurers were selectively buying equities based on higher dividend yields, as equities were the only financial instruments they can use to hedge against inflation.
He also said major institutional investors were buying equities by selectively focusing on return on equity (ROE).
